source: Supreme Court of India, order of 10 March 2026
note: Paragraph 10 recalls the order of 24 February 2026 that the judicial officers' orders could not be appealed before an executive or administrative officer. Paragraph 11 provides for tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges, to be notified by the Commission in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court at Calcutta.

source: Supreme Court of India, order of 13 April 2026
note: The tribunals were to begin work on 13 April 2026. Appeals decided by 21 and 27 April were to take effect through a supplementary roll before polling, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
The Court declined to take up fresh grievances and gave liberty to approach the Chief Justice of the High Court.
The paper reports that the judges refused to log in to the Commission's new portal from 21 September.
A source told the paper, in its report of 21 November 2026, that orders were being uploaded again from 6 November, after a gap of nearly 45 days.

The bench directed the tribunals to hear the appeals of deleted electors first and to defer appeals against inclusion, and directed the Commission, with the Chief Justice of the High Court, to increase the strength of the tribunals.
